topic: Review and perspective on ITER plasma control requirements: model-based design, state observers, exception handling, forecasting, and actuator sharing
own_question: Which aspects of ITER plasma control differ from present devices, and what physics and mathematics research remains open?
actual_method_and_evidence: Narrative review. It illustrates points with prior results from other works (JET q-profile control, DIII-D feedforward/feedback, AUG and DIII-D divertor control, an ITER Catch-and-Subdue simulation, and RAPTOR on TCV/AUG). It reports no new validated experiment. CES, ion temperature, BES/ECEI and nowcasting are not addressed.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: Model-based state observers, such as Kalman-type filters, combine real-time measurements with model-based prior expectations to give a single state estimate. This can reduce a controller's reliance on any individual diagnostic.
claim_checks.qualification: This is a conceptual description in a review, not demonstrated performance. The source discusses q and kinetic profiles, not CES impurity temperature.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: ITER control planning envisions real-time plasma state estimation and forecasting as support functions, although the detailed scope was stated as still to be defined.
claim_checks.qualification: These are planned requirements, not an achieved deployment. Fig. 19 was not visually checked.

input_target_timing_if_relevant: Not relevant to CES report timing. Lead times mentioned (~10 ms for gas injection, longer for equilibrium changes) concern disruption mitigation and must not be transferred to our setting.
forbidden_inferences: Do not cite it as evidence about CES or Ti nowcasting.
Do not present ITER requirements as achieved performance.
Do not imply it shows BES/ECEI information gain.
Do not treat the RAPTOR description as validation of our estimator.
Do not use it to claim prior work is noncausal.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Optional background citation for motivating the concept of real-time state estimation. It is not a methodological precedent for our study.
